newsitem.title: TURKEY: Sixty-one Kurd rebels killed in Turkish clashes.
newsitem.headline: Sixty-one Kurd rebels killed in Turkish clashes.

text.p: Seven Turkish soldiers and 61 Kurdish rebels were killed in clashes in four provinces in eastern and southeastern Turkey, security officials said on Saturday.

The emergency rule governor's office in Diyarbakir said troops killed 33 rebels of the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) in the eastern province of Van, which borders Iran, and 28 in the southeastern provinces of Sirnak, Hakkari and Mardin.
Seven soldiers were killed in the clashes that took place overnight or on Saturday.
Clashes in Van -- where guerrillas sometimes cross over from Iran -- have been on the rise recently.

Turkey accuses neighbours Iran and Syria of sponsoring the PKK but Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said during a visit to Iran last month that Tehran assured him it was not supporting the separatist group.

The PKK also uses northern Iraq as a base for its attacks on Turkey and Ankara said this month it wants to set up a security zone just inside Iraq to keep the guerrillas out. Iraq, which recently intervened in north Iraq to help a Kurdish faction rout a rival group, strongly opposes the idea.
More than 20,000 people have been killed in the 12-year-old struggle between the Turkish army and the PKK, which is fighting for self-rule in Turkey's mainly Kurdish southeast.
